answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the basalt identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator pays for 323 runs and collects one. Because the pearl index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the anchor audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 323 answers need 323 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
